page: Microsoft Azure L16as_v4 is a storage and memory-optimized server instance belonging to the Lasv4 family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz, delivering 16 virtual CPUs across 8 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and features 3840 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability. The instance operates on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25 percent. Text processing performance is highly competitive, ranking in the top 10 percent of tested instances. Multi-core CPU performance, database operations, and static web serving throughput fall within the average range. However, memory bandwidth exhibits a notable bottleneck, with uncached large-block read operations registering in the bottom 25 percent, while small-block cached reads maintain average speeds.

Given the high local storage capacity of 3840 GB and a 1 to 8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the L16as_v4 is structured for data-intensive workloads, relational databases, and caching layers. The dedicated AMD EPYC cores provide stable compute resources, though the lower large-block read memory bandwidth suggests it is less optimal for massive in-memory analytics that frequently bypass the cache. The instance offers a balanced cost-to-resource profile for storage-heavy deployments that require substantial local disk space without the overhead of external storage attachments.

Operating on the x86_64 architecture via Microsoft Hyper-V, this instance delivers strong single-core and text-processing performance, though its multi-core and database operations fall in the average tier. With its high local storage capacity and a 1 to 8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the L16as_v4 is highly suited for database hosting, caching layers, and storage-intensive applications that benefit from dedicated CPU resources and large local disk capacity without requiring GPU acceleration.
